headline: Metal avalanche on the Brenner: Tyrolean resistance against traffic
lead: Millions of vehicles roll over the Brenner Pass in Tyrol every year. The traffic is so burdensome for the narrow valley that resistance is forming. Our correspondent was on site.
seo_title: Brenner Pass: Protest against traffic jams in Tyrol
social_title: Traffic jam at the Brenner Pass: Resistance to the traffic is growing
print_title: The traffic jam: Tyrol's fight against traffic collapse
print_subtitle: Tyroleans block Brenner motorway: Protest against traffic avalanche.
summary_bullets_en: Millions of vehicles cross the Brenner Pass annually, causing significant traffic issues and strain on the narrow Tyrolean valley.
At the end of May, over 4,000 people protested on the Brenner motorway to highlight the impact of diverted traffic and the difficult situation for residents in places like Matrei and Gries.

original_de.lead: Millionen von Fahrzeugen rollen jedes Jahr über den Brennerpass in Tirol. Der Verkehr ist für das enge Tal so belastend, dass sich Widerstand formiert. Unsere Korrespondentin war vor Ort.

body.text: _Listen and subscribe to the podcast «NZZ Akzent» on Spotify, Apple Podcasts, or Castbox._

At the end of May, more than 4,000 people marched on the Brenner highway in Tyrol. They paralyzed traffic. The «traffic jam of the century» some feared for the Whitsun weekend was prevented, but the participants of the demonstration certainly captured the attention of many.

Especially in Germany, the Brenner is a synonym for holidays in Italy for many. It is the last stage that must be completed, preferably without traffic jams or slow-moving traffic. But that is becoming increasingly difficult. «The numbers continue to rise,» explains Austria correspondent Meret Baumann. She was in the Wipptal, through which the A 13 runs, and says that the protest drew attention to the situation of the residents, but the so-called «traffic jam refugees» still come. The diversion traffic from the congested highway brings noise, hardly any paying customers, and severely impedes the people in Matrei or Gries am Brenner. Even ambulances often do not reach their destination.
_All episodes of «NZZ Akzent» can be found in this overview._
